'''Matthew Phillip Hardy''' (1957-2007) was an American [[reproductive medicine|reproductive biologist]] who has made fundamental contributions in [[Leydig cell]] [[Cellular differentiation|differentiation]] and function.<ref name="In Memoriam"/>

== Biography ==
M. P. Hardy was born in [[Evanston, Illinois]], completed elementary education at the [[Sidwell Friends School]] in [[Washington, DC]]. He received a double bachelor's degree in biology and philosophy from [[Oberlin College]] in 1979, and received a Ph.D. in Biology at the [[University of Virginia]] in 1985. Then Hardy conducted postdoctoral work with [[Larry L. Ewing]] at The [[Johns Hopkins School of Hygiene and Public Health]].<ref>{{cite journal |author=Matthew P Hardy |author2=Barry R Zirkin |author3=Larry L Ewing | title=Kinetic studies on the development of the adult population of Leydig cells in testes of the pubertal rat | journal=[[Endocrinology]]  | volume=142 | issue=2 | year= 1989 | pages= 762–70  |doi = 10.1210/endo-124-2-762 | pmid=2912699}}</ref> In 1990, he joined the [[Population Council]], and became a Senior Scientist several years later.<ref name="In Memoriam">{{cite journal |author=Barry R Zirkin |author2=Peter Schlegel |author3=Bernard Robaire |author4=Sally Perreault | title=In Memoriam Matthew P. Hardy, Ph.D. 1957–2007 | journal=[[Biology of Reproduction]]  | volume=78 | issue=3| year=2008 | pages= 563–564 |doi = 10.1095/biolreprod.108.067983 | doi-access=free }}</ref>

Hardy's research focus on the origin and development of [[Leydig cells]] in the adult [[mammalian]] [[testis]], which from stem Leydig cells (SLC) to progenitor Leydig cells (PLC) to immature Leydig cells (ILC) and finally to adult Leydig cells (ALC). He identified this sequence in detail in morphological, physiological, biochemical and molecular methodologies.<ref name="pmid18184909">{{cite journal |vauthors=Dong L, Jelinsky SA, Finger JN, Johnston DS, Kopf GS, Sottas CM, Hardy MP, Ge RS |title=Gene expression during development of fetal and adult Leydig cells |journal=[[Annals of the New York Academy of Sciences]]  |volume=1120 |issue=1 |date=December 2007 |pages=16–35 |doi=10.1196/annals.1411.016 |pmid=18184909|bibcode=2007NYASA1120...16D |s2cid=25978550 }}</ref> He also revealed the role of [[luteinizing hormone]] (LH) in the androgenesis of adult Leydig cells.<ref name="In Memoriam"/>

He died suddenly after accomplishing the 2007 [[New York City Marathon]].<ref name="In Memoriam"/>
